lines: StoneX macro strategist Vincent Deluard reads the US midterms as part of a global turn to economic populism, with voters focused on inflation and affordability over cultural issues, and notes that huge campaign spending failed to sway key races.
He argues the 2% inflation target is becoming untenable under fiscal dominance: central banks will have to tolerate structurally higher inflation to fund swelling government deficits.

Deluard sees an emerging 'national capitalism' in which countries repatriate capital from US markets to pay for energy independence, infrastructure and defense, a long-term threat to US equity and bond valuations that depend on foreign inflows.
He says the Mexican 'super peso' is fading on lower remittances, tighter border enforcement and the unwinding of the yen carry trade, while Canada looks more resilient thanks to pragmatic management.
He also contends subscription models and algorithmic personalized pricing shift welfare from consumers to producers and make inflation harder to measure, feeding discontent and polarization.
title: The Return of Economic Populism and the End of Two Percent | Vincent Deluard
